html:
The bandeirantes were armed expeditions from São Paulo that went deep into the interior of South America in the 1600s and 1700s to capture Indigenous slaves and search for gold and gems.

São Paulo was poor and far from the sugar coast. Its settlers, many of mixed Portuguese and Tupi descent who spoke the Tupi língua geral, marched for months or years through forest and plains. They raided the Jesuit missions of the Guaraní in the 1620s and 1630s, enslaving tens of thousands. They also helped destroy Palmares in 1694.

In the 1690s they found gold in Minas Gerais, starting the Brazilian gold rush. Their journeys carried Portuguese claims far west of the old treaty line, and the treaty of 1750 recognised much of this, giving Brazil its huge size. São Paulo honours them as pioneers; others see them as slave hunters.
sum: The bandeirantes were armed expeditions from São Paulo that went deep into the interior of South America in the 1600s and 1700s to capture Indigenous slaves and search for gold and gems.
